verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents its own background automation for flag releases. Guarded rollouts raise traffic on their own while monitoring metrics for regressions until they reach 100%. Scheduled flag changes apply targeting edits at future points in time, and marketing describes Autopilot rolling back broken releases. These automations are limited to flag release workflows, and scheduling is shown only as one-off future changes, not recurring schedules. missing for 10: general-purpose user-defined automations beyond flag releases, evidence of recurring schedules, documented detail on adaptive triggers and Autopilot, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: A guarded rollout progressively increases traffic to the new variation while monitoring selected metrics for regressions until the rollout reaches 100%.
Scheduling flag changes lets you define and schedule changes to your flag's targeting rules for future points in time.
Autopilot ships it safely, and rolls it back if it breaks.
